name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Stutzman renominated with large fundraising edge
No public polling and no expert ratings on the race
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 4%
model.rationale: The R+16 district, an incumbent with a roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing Democrats at about 4% all point to a safe Republican hold; the modest Democratic environment is not enough to close a double-digit structural gap.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a polling error in the Republican direction could tighten the race, but no evidence of either has appeared.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northeast Indiana's third district is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about sixteen points toward the GOP. Marlin Stutzman returns as the incumbent after winning renomination, holding a large financial edge over Democrat Kelly Thompson, who has raised little and has minimal cash on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Stutzman and nothing against him.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. The district's lean, incumbency, and money gap make a Republican hold the clear expectation, with only a modest Democratic tail risk from a favorable national environment.
